system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m cap. | 25% / AUD 6m general Warranty cap. | **Reject; restore AUD 6m.** The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft; none exists. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Replace both thresholds and basket mechanics.** Seller’s proposal materially excludes otherwise recoverable claims. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months after Completion for general Warranty Claims, without overriding separate regimes. | **Restore 24 months and remove the blanket extension.** The 18-month fallback lacks Amelia Frost’s required written approval. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate 100% cap; at least six years; outside general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. | **Reject general-regime treatment; draft express exclusions.** Ownership and capacity risks require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims, without an express carve-out. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding carve-out throughout.** This protection is mandatory and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Specific fair disclosure sufficient to identify each matter’s nature and scope; no blanket or deemed disclosure. | **Reject general disclosures as warranty qualifications.** Document availability and prudent searches do not substitute for specific fair disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters discoverable from data-room or public-record searches. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any retained knowledge qualifier must use named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 and resist constructive knowledge.** It improperly transfers undisclosed-risk responsibility to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although no final consent or conditions evidence is supplied. | Effective consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Retain a substantive Completion condition.** Delivery alone is insufficient for a customer representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion; no repayment or final discharge supplied. | Current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. | **Require coordinated repayment and release at Completion.** Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval, neither presently established. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses omitted from funds flow; applicable on-costs unspecified. | Express line item or seller funding for bonuses triggered by Completion/continued employment, plus triggered on-costs. | **Correct funds flow and confirm payroll treatment.** Calling bonuses a Seller matter does not prevent an unfunded Company liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 shown open, without independent payment verification or confirmatory assignment. | Broader protection for related IP ownership/transfer defects and resulting losses, preserving the SOW3 payment-and-transfer cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment and title transfer.** The narrow payment protection does not resolve wider IP risk; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said unlikely to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, require updates and assess legal obligations on evidence. | **Maintain investigation and reporting protections; reserve conclusions.** Neither a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty nor any numeric demand is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate treated as ordinary-course operating costs, despite unresolved timing, scope and commitment status. | Assess all three renewals together, including accrual, avoidability, termination rights and ordinary-course status. | **Investigate before agreeing treatment; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The disclosed amount alone does not determine price-mechanics treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations and remedies extend across all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants separate, with express treatment and no hidden general-regime override. | **Replace blanket cross-application with clear category-specific provisions.** General limitations must not silently dilute separately negotiated rights. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s Company share register recording Seller ownership of 100%. | Independent evidence of ownership, title, absence of encumbrances and authority to sell. | **Require independent verification before Completion.** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Treats tax and IP warranty positions as settled under the general regime. | Keep both sets of terms expressly open for negotiation, with their treatment separately agreed. | **Reject the asserted settlement and reserve both categories.** Neither resolution nor unlimited liability may be assumed. |
=== END ADVICE ===
